question: The radius of a circle is 12.5 cm and the length of one its chords is 11 cm. What is the distance of the chord from the centre? (correct to one decimal place)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Half of the chord length = 11 ÷ 2 = 5.5 cm.

Using Pythagoras theorem to find the distance (d) from the centre directly:

d = √(12.5² − 5.5²) = √[(12.5 + 5.5) × (12.5 − 5.5)]

d = √(18 × 7) = √126 ≈ 11.22 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 11.2 cm.**
